content.subject: Proposed jury instructions for the defective-appliance case
content.body:
Hi,

As we get closer to trial in my product-liability matter, I have been doing some reading on how juries get told what the law is, and I gather that proposed jury instructions are a really important part of the trial preparation. I would like to be more involved in that piece of the case than I have been so far.

Would the firm be willing to prepare a draft set of proposed jury instructions for my case and send them to me to review? I would like each proposed instruction to include the supporting authority right beneath it, with proper citations to the controlling case law, the pattern instructions, and any statutory or regulatory sources that back up the language being proposed. If a particular instruction tracks an existing pattern with modifications, please cite the pattern and note where you have departed from it and why, with the supporting citations for the departure.

I know this is a lot of work, and I am happy to pay for the time. I would rather see the legal scaffolding behind each instruction now, before trial, so I can ask questions intelligently, than be handed a clean version at the last minute.

Thanks for considering this.

Warmly,
Philippa Cresswell
